institution: Huawei Noah's Ark Lab, London, UK (verified in fetched text)
tiering: EM-LLM divides context into three groups: 'initial tokens, evicted tokens, and local context.' The 128 initial tokens act as fixed attention sinks; evicted tokens are managed by the proposed memory model 'functioning similarly to short-term episodic memory in the brain'; local context uses full softmax attention, likened to the 'focus of attention' in working memory.
write_path: Tokens are segmented online during inference: a token becomes a candidate event boundary WHEN its surprise (negative log-likelihood of the ground-truth token) exceeds a moving threshold T. Boundaries are then refined by an algorithm maximizing modularity / minimizing conductance over the attention-key similarity graph. No separate LLM-summary, fact-extraction, or importance-scoring step is used; the KV cache itself is grouped into event units.
consolidation_trigger: Streaming/online, threshold-based: 'a token x_t is considered a potential boundary if its surprise value exceeds a threshold T', with T computed from a moving window of surprise mean/variance — there is no periodic or offline ('sleep-time') consolidation phase; segmentation and refinement occur continuously as tokens are processed.
consolidation_cadence: No fixed time interval is stated; threshold T=μ(t−τ)+γσ(t−τ) adapts via window offset τ and scaling factor γ. For the PG-19 experiments the paper reports the hyperparameter: 'Surprise threshold = 0.001 0.001 0.001'. Short-context evaluation uses a '4K+2K' context split.
what_is_consolidated: Raw KV-cache token spans are grouped into 'episodic events' via surprise-based segmentation, then boundaries are refined using graph-clustering metrics (modularity Eq.3, conductance Eq.4) over an adjacency matrix of attention-key similarities, optimizing intra-event cohesion and inter-event separation — this is token-group clustering, not summarization, fact extraction, or semantic graph-building of extracted facts.
decay_or_tombstone: No decay/forgetting of the episodic memory store itself is specified. Only the retrieval-time 'contiguity buffer' (a queue of size k_c) decays: 'The queue structure allows for a natural decay of temporal context as new events are processed, with older or repeated events being dequeued as new ones are added.'
decay_formula: not specified in paper
capacity_and_eviction: 128 initial tokens are always retained as attention sinks ('we also maintain a group of 128 initial tokens in the LLM context'). At retrieval, k = k_s + k_c + 2 events are added to the context window (k_s similarity-buffer events, k_c-sized contiguity queue). No explicit cap on total evicted-token/episodic-memory store size is given.

institution: China Mobile Digital Intelligence Business Unit / China Mobile Jiutian Research Institute (verified on fetched PDF page 1)
tiering: Three layers: Sensory Memory Layer ("instantaneous registration and preliminary screening of sensory inputs", retention milliseconds to seconds), Working Memory Layer ("typical capacity of 7±2 items", duration seconds to minutes, cleared on task completion), and Long-Term Memory Layer ("persistent storage layer houses consolidated knowledge" with continuous importance-based pruning).
write_path: Working memory holds actively processed task information; upon task completion, contents are "either consolidated into long-term memory (if deemed important) or automatically cleared". Long-term memory undergoes continuous evaluation via the ImportanceScoringEngine (CQA, BVE, TRS, SRC) rather than a specified single-turn write trigger.
consolidation_trigger: Threshold/capacity-triggered: consolidation into long-term memory occurs at task completion, and forgetting is triggered when capacity is exceeded — "After each batch, the SelectiveForgettingMechanism checked capacity usage. If the limit was exceeded, it triggered a pruning cycle based on the priority queue of importance scores."
consolidation_cadence: Batch processing in groups of 100 records ("Data was processed in small batches (100 records)"); capacity constraint set at 70% ("FSFM System: Operated under a strict 70% capacity constraint"); pruning batch size tuned among 5%, 10%, 20%, with "Pruning 10% was optimal".
what_is_consolidated: Working memory items deemed important are consolidated into long-term memory; no raw-to-summary or episodic-to-semantic transformation, clustering, or graph-building process is described for this consolidation step beyond the importance-based retain/clear decision.
decay_or_tombstone: Yes — passive decay-based forgetting using time-dependent decay functions inspired by the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve, extended with a reinforcement function incorporating frequency, emotional valence, contextual relevance, etc.; low-scoring items are pruned rather than described as tombstoned.
decay_formula: Traditional: Retention(t)=e^{-\lambda t}, where Retention(t) is probability of successful retrieval at time t, \lambda is the decay rate parameter (varies by memory type/importance), t is time since last reinforcement. FSFM Enhanced: Retention(t)=e^{-\lambda t} \times f(frequency, emotional_valence, contextual_relevance, ...). TRS component: "Calculated as e^(-\lambda t) * usage_frequency". Example rates used: \lambda=0.1 (classical baseline), \lambda=0.85 (low-value memory), tuning range \lambda=0.05 (long-term) to \lambda=0.2 (transient), tested from 0.01 to 0.5.
capacity_and_eviction: "FSFM System: Operated under a strict 70% capacity constraint. When new data was added, the SelectiveForgettingMechanism pruned low-importance records to stay within this limit." Baseline System operated with unlimited capacity. Formally, given capacity constraint C (70% of storage) and total N (100%), the optimal forgetting set F = arg min \sum_{i \in F} s_i subject to |M-F| \leq C.

institution: Stanford University (verified in fetched text: 'Joon Sung Park Stanford University')
tiering: The paper names a single overarching store, the 'memory stream,' holding three object types retrieved together: observations (raw perceived events), reflections ('a second type of memory' that is 'higher-level, more abstract'), and plans (future action sequences). write_path: Observations are written every sandbox time step as a natural-language action statement (e.g. 'Isabella Rodriguez is writing in her journal'); each memory object gets a creation timestamp, most-recent-access timestamp, and an LLM-generated importance score at creation. Reflections and plans are also written back into the memory stream once generated.
consolidation_trigger: Threshold-triggered, not streaming or scheduled offline: reflections are generated 'periodically' specifically 'when the sum of the importance scores for the latest events perceived by the agents exceeds a threshold.'
consolidation_cadence: Threshold value of 150 on summed importance scores triggers reflection; empirically 'our agents reflected roughly two or three times a day.' The reflection-question step queries 'the 100 most recent records in the agent's memory stream.'
what_is_consolidated: Recent observations (and prior reflections) are used to generate salient questions, retrieve related memories, and have the LLM produce high-level insights citing supporting records, building a recursive 'reflection tree' where 'the leaf nodes...represent the base observations, and the non-leaf nodes represent thoughts that become more abstract.'
decay_or_tombstone: A decay function exists for retrieval ranking only, not for deleting memories: recency 'is an exponential decay function over the number of sandbox game hours since the memory was last retrieved.' decay_formula: Recency decays with decay factor 0.995 per sandbox game hour since last retrieval; final retrieval score is score = α_recency·recency + α_importance·importance + α_relevance·relevance, with 'all αs are set to 1' after min-max normalization to [0,1].
capacity_and_eviction: not specified in paper — no size cap or eviction rule for the memory stream itself is given; the only bound described is retrieval-side: 'the top-ranked memories that fit within the language model's context window are included in the prompt.'

institution: Vectorize.io, USA (verified on fetched PDF page 1; co-authors The Washington Post, Virginia Tech)
tiering: Four named memory networks partition the bank M={W,B,O,S}: the world network (objective external facts), the experience/'bank' network (first-person agent experiences), the opinion network (subjective judgments as tuples (t,c,τ) with confidence c), and the observation network (preference-neutral entity summaries synthesized from world+experience facts). write_path: Retain(B,D)→M′: on ingestion of conversational transcripts/documents D, 'TEMPR uses an open-source LLM to convert conversational transcripts into narrative facts and associated metadata,' extracting 2–5 coarse-grained narrative facts per conversation, classifying each into world/experience/opinion/observation, building graph links, and reinforcing existing opinions when new evidence arrives.
consolidation_trigger: Two triggered (not periodic) mechanisms: (1) observation regeneration fires whenever new facts mentioning an entity are retained ('a background task is triggered to recompute o_e'), running asynchronously; (2) opinion reinforcement fires 'when new facts arrive via TEMPR's retain pathway.' consolidation_cadence: No time-based interval given; cadence is per-conversation: 'extracting 2–5 comprehensive facts per conversation.' RRF fusion uses an example constant k=60. Recall token budgets are per-benchmark but left as unfilled placeholders ('<add> tokens') in the text.

institution: not stated in fetched text (ICML-format page 1 shows numeric affiliation markers without institution names; code repo is github.com/IBM/larimar)
tiering: Larimar follows a Complementary Learning Systems view: a hippocampal-like fast-learning episodic memory (fixed-size matrix M with K rows) stores encoded episodes, while the LLM decoder acts as the neocortical slow-learning semantic system. An optional scope detector further separates in-scope queries (memory-conditioned decoding) from out-of-scope queries (unconditioned decoding).
write_path: At inference time, an incoming episode/fact is encoded by encoder e into Z, then written to memory in one-shot by solving a least-squares/pseudo-inverse update (no gradient training): 'During inference, the new data is written to memory in one-shot, the updated memory then conditions the LLM decoding to enforce the edited output.' There is no per-turn logging or session-end summarization described.
consolidation_trigger: Writing is event-triggered per edit/episode (one-shot at inference), not periodic, threshold-based, or offline/sleep-time: memory is updated immediately 'during inference' each time new data or an edit arrives, via the sequential update equations (Eq. 3-4).
consolidation_cadence: No time-based schedule; cadence is one update per incoming episode/edit. Memory size K is set proportional to expected number of facts, e.g. K=1000 for sequential ZsRE editing ('we use K = 1000 ... setting the memory size proportional to the number of facts to be written') and K=512 in batch/forgetting experiments.
what_is_consolidated: Encoded episodes (Z, encoder outputs of facts/text) are folded directly into the memory matrix M via a recursive least-squares/Bayesian update (Eq. 3-4); there is no raw-to-summary compression, clustering, or graph-building step — 'Eq. (4) updates the memory sequentially such that it remains the least-squares solution for the growing sequence of data.'
decay_or_tombstone: Yes, an explicit training-free forgetting operation: a previously written encoding is removed from the least-squares memory solution by rewriting it with a negative update coefficient, enabling selective forgetting while other facts are retained, as shown by 'Larimar can selectively forget using the memory updating mechanism, while retaining the remaining knowledge, whereas in-context learning struggles.'
decay_formula: Sequential update: C_i = C_{i-1} + α_i·W_i^T W_i and M_i = M_{i-1} + α_i·C_i^{-1} W_i^T (Z_i − W_i M_{i-1}) (Eqs. 3-4). Writing a new fact uses α_i=1; forgetting a previously written encoding uses α_i=−1 at a later step, which provably removes that encoding's contribution to the least-squares solution.
capacity_and_eviction: Memory has a fixed number of rows K (e.g., K=512 or K=1000 depending on experiment). Beyond capacity, recall degrades rather than triggering explicit eviction: 'the rewrite accuracy is near 100% for up to 512 edits (the memory size K) and then drops to 82% for 1024 edits,' showing compression of more than K facts into the size-K memory.

institution: Kennesaw State University (verified in fetched text; single author Ying Xie)
tiering: The paper does not name distinct memory tiers (e.g., short-term vs long-term store). It uses a single 'augmented cache' extending the standard KV cache, 𝒞+ = {(k_i,v_i,τ_i,s_i,σ_i,a_i)}, whose entries can be tagged Keep, Compress, or Evict; Compress-marked entries are merged into consolidated summary entries within the same cache rather than moved to a separate store.
write_path: Every token: the transformer's own forward pass produces (k_t,v_t) which is appended to the augmented cache tagged with timestamp τ_i, a computed semantic signature s_i, superseded flag σ_i (initially 0), and cumulative attention a_i. 'During the wake phase, the model processes input tokens while maintaining a tagged KV cache.' This is done by the model/tagger process itself, not an LLM summary.
consolidation_trigger: Adaptive/threshold trigger, not purely periodic or purely streaming: a sleep micro-cycle fires when attention entropy exceeds a running threshold, OR conflict density (fraction of superseded entries) exceeds ρ_max, OR as a periodic fallback: 'the last term provides a fallback periodic trigger every N max tokens.'
consolidation_cadence: Fallback periodic interval N_max = 128 tokens; conflict-density threshold ρ_max = 0.4 ('Trigger when 40% superseded'); entropy threshold uses κ = 1.5 standard deviations above the mean. Steady-state cache size example: for eviction fraction f_e=0.3 and per-cluster compression ratio c=4, bound is |C'+| ≤ 1.67N.
what_is_consolidated: Entries assigned the Compress action are clustered by cosine similarity of semantic signatures (new cluster if similarity < δ/2), then merged into one consolidated key-value pair per cluster via a weighted average key and a recency-biased weighted-sum value (Eq. 12), 'analogous to hippocampal replay transferring episodic memories into semantic knowledge.'
decay_or_tombstone: Yes: an explicit 'Key Decay (Synaptic Downscaling)' phase exponentially/log-scale decays key vectors by age every cycle, followed by a learned forgetting gate that marks entries Keep/Compress/Evict; the hard-eviction variant permanently removes Evict-marked entries (tombstone-like), while the soft-biasing variant exponentially suppresses (but does not delete) stale entries via an attention bias.
decay_formula: k_i ← k_i · (1+age_i)^{-λ}, where age_i = t_current − τ_i and λ is the decay rate, set to λ = 0.01 in the experiments (Appendix Table 3, 'Decay rate ... 0.01 ... Log-scale key decay rate').
capacity_and_eviction: For SleepGate itself, steady-state cache size is bounded: |C'+| ≤ N/(f_e+(1-f_e)(1-1/c)); with f_e=0.3, c=4 this gives ≤1.67N, 'a substantial reduction from the unbounded growth of the standard KV cache.' A compared baseline (Sliding Window) is capped at a 'Fixed window of 64 entries; oldest entries are discarded.' Hard eviction removes entries with retention r_i < α_e = 0.3.

update_ops: Six tools exposed to the agent as actions, split by target: LTM gets Add / Update / Delete; STM gets Retrieve / Summary / Filter. This is the only system in the track that puts short-term context management (summarize, filter) into the same learned operation set as long-term writes. Appendix A.1 gives set semantics: Add unions a new (content, embedding, metadata) triple; Update replaces content, embedding and metadata in place with a modification timestamp; Delete removes the entry.
who_decides: Learned RL policy over a tool-based action space — the agent's own policy, not a separate manager. Trained with a three-stage progressive strategy (LTM construction, then STM management under distractors, then joint) and a step-wise GRPO designed for the sparse, discontinuous rewards memory operations induce. Reward is a weighted sum R(tau) = sum w_i*R_i(tau) + P_penalty(tau) where R_i covers task performance and memory quality and P_penalty discourages redundant storage, excessive tool calls and uncontrolled context expansion. All reward weights are set to 1.0 without manual tuning. The paper's stated motivation is removing dependence on an auxiliary expert LLM for memory control.
contradiction_resolution: Rule semantics, learned invocation. Update is defined as the operation invoked when new information supersedes or refines previous knowledge, and Delete removes obsolete or incorrect memories — both destructive in-place with a modification timestamp; no versioning or invalidation. Which to invoke is learned from the reward rather than judged by a prompt.
ranking_signals: Cosine similarity only, stated as used for semantic matching throughout the framework. Retrieve returns TopK by cosine; Filter removes context messages by the same similarity measure.
ranking_combination: Single signal, no combination. The adaptivity is in when and with what k the agent invokes Retrieve, not in how candidates are scored.
injection_budget: k is a tool parameter the agent chooses, typically set to 3-5 in their experiments to balance relevance against context size — the tightest stated injection budget in the track. The reward's penalty term additionally punishes uncontrolled context expansion, so the budget is partly learned. Realized token counts appear in the reward ablation: Answer-Only 2078 tokens vs All-Returns 2117.

update_ops: Real-time incremental update with three effective operations: update-or-create session summary (refine keywords/themes for an ongoing session, create a new summary for a new session), extract-and-deduplicate triples, and establish cross-level hyperlinks among summaries, triples and chunks. who_decides: Fixed rules plus LLM extraction. Duplicate detection is type-aware and semantic-similarity matching — a rule, not a judge. Summary refinement and triple extraction are LLM operations but no operation-selection judge or learned policy exists.
contradiction_resolution: Deduplication rather than contradiction handling. On detecting a duplicate triple the system attaches the new source as an additional hyperlink to the existing node instead of creating a new node — a merge-by-reference that keeps the graph compact. Genuine contradiction is not addressed; the mechanism that partly compensates is the temporal decay in ranking, which down-weights (but never invalidates) older triples.
ranking_signals: Three factors, all combined at read time: session-level relevance S_s (query entities matched against session summary keys by overlap and semantic similarity), triple-level relevance S_t, and temporal relevance via a recency decay.
ranking_combination: Fully specified formula, the most explicit in the track. Semantic relevance is the HARMONIC MEAN of the two similarity levels: S_sem = 2*S_s*S_t/(S_s+S_t). Temporal weight is a Weibull decay w(dt) = exp[-(dt/tau_hat)^k] with 0<k<1, where tau_hat is the MEDIAN of time gaps across retrieved triples, making the decay adapt per query. Final score is multiplicative: R(t) = S_sem * w(dt). The paper argues explicitly that because w is in (0,1] time modulates rather than dominates the semantic signal. Note: k is constrained but no numeric value for k is given in the fetched text.
injection_budget: Not specified as a numeric k or token cap. The output is a structured prompt consolidating relevant session summaries, top-ranked triples and their source chunks; 'top-ranked' is not quantified in the fetched text. Efficiency is reported as query latency instead.
associative_links: Yes — three-layer hierarchical graph (session summary / entity-relation triple / raw chunk) wired by explicit hyperlinks, with bidirectional traceability between raw text and structured knowledge. Reward is outcome-driven and defined exactly: R_answer = EM(y_pred, y_gold), the exact match of a FROZEN Answer Agent's prediction against ground truth after the memory operation is applied. Individual edits are never scored; only the downstream QA consequence is. The Answer Agent is frozen during Memory Manager training to avoid attribution ambiguity. A second RL-trained component, the Answer Agent with a Memory Distillation policy, learns to filter retrieved memories.

update_ops: Two operations, named by function not by keyword: memory addition and memory merge, executed at session end by Prospective Reflection. Each extracted topic-based memory is compared against Top-K semantically similar bank entries and either directly added (new topic) or merged into an updated entry (updated information on a discussed topic). No delete and no NOOP.
who_decides: Split decision — this is the distinguishing design. WRITE side: an LLM judge (prompt in Appendix D.1.2) decides add vs merge. READ side: a learned RL policy — a lightweight reranker trained online with REINFORCE.
contradiction_resolution: Merge, not overwrite or invalidate. When an extracted memory provides updated information on a previously discussed topic it is merged with the existing memory into a single updated one. No versioning, no time bounds, no record that the earlier value was ever held.
ranking_signals: Dense retriever (Contriever by default; Stella and GTE also evaluated) producing Top-K candidates, then a learned reranker over query and memory embeddings with linear layers plus residual connections and Gumbel-trick stochastic sampling of relevance scores, selecting Top-M. Recency/importance are not used as signals.
ranking_combination: Two-stage cascade with a learned second stage: retriever Top-K -> reranker Top-M. The reranker's learning signal is citation-based: each retrieved memory gets reward +1 if the generator cites it in the final response, -1 otherwise, and the reranker is updated by REINFORCE with delta_phi = eta*(R-b)*grad log P(M_M|q,M_K;phi), b a hyperparameter baseline. Notably the reward comes from the generator's own citations in a single LLM call, produced conditioned on the response — no labelled data.
injection_budget: Stated numerically. Without a reranker, Top-K = 5. With the reranker, default Top-K = 20 and Top-M = 5. The appendix also reports Top-K = 50 / Top-M = 10, which improves both recall and accuracy (GTE: 69.8 -> 74.4 recall, 70.4 -> 73.8 accuracy).

ranking_combination: Set union with deduplication, and the paper argues against weighting explicitly: results from the three views are merged by set union, which naturally deduplicates, 'balancing structural constraints and semantic relevance without complex linear weighting'. Deduplication is ID-based. This is the clearest anti-weighted-fusion position in the track.
injection_budget: Adaptive rather than fixed. An LLM planner infers latent search intent and emits optimized per-view queries plus an adaptive retrieval depth d; a candidate limit n proportional to d is imposed on each of the three retrieval paths, explicitly to balance recall against context-window constraints. No fixed k. Realized: 530-580 tokens per query on average, 531 on GPT-4.1-mini.

provenance: Symbolic layer stores structured metadata including timestamps and entity types; no source pointer or provenance surfacing is described.

update_ops: No ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP vocabulary. Operations are graph-write primitives: entity extraction with a reflexion-style refinement pass, entity resolution/dedup against candidate nodes, edge extraction, edge deduplication constrained to the same entity pair, temporal extraction, and edge invalidation. Writes are explicitly non-lossy — nothing is deleted; superseded facts are time-bounded.
who_decides: LLM judge for the semantic decisions (entity resolution, contradiction detection between new and existing edges), but graph writes use predefined Cypher queries rather than LLM-generated queries, a choice the paper justifies as reducing hallucination. No learned policy anywhere.
contradiction_resolution: Bi-temporal edge invalidation — the most explicit mechanism in the track. Four timestamps per edge: t'created / t'expired on the transactional timeline (when the system learned/retracted it) and t_valid / t_invalid on the world timeline (when the fact actually held). An LLM compares a new edge against semantically related existing edges; on a temporally overlapping contradiction the affected edge's t_invalid is set to the invalidating edge's t_valid. New information always wins on the transactional timeline. The old edge remains queryable — history is preserved, not overwritten.
ranking_signals: Three parallel search functions: cosine semantic similarity, Okapi BM25 full-text (both via Neo4j/Lucene), and breadth-first graph search. Applied over three object types with different search fields — semantic edges (fact field), entity nodes (name), community nodes (community name).
ranking_combination: Explicit three-stage composition f(a) = chi(rho(phi(a))): search (phi, high recall) -> reranker (rho, precision) -> constructor (chi, text context). Reranker is pluggable, not a fixed weighted sum: Reciprocal Rank Fusion, Maximal Marginal Relevance, an episode-mentions reranker keyed on entity/fact mention frequency, a node-distance reranker keyed on graph distance from a centroid node, and cross-encoder LLM reranking (named as highest quality and highest cost). No weight values are stated.
injection_budget: No stated top-k or token cap in the retrieval design. The realized budget is reported in Table 2: Zep averages 1.6k context tokens vs 115k for full-context on LongMemEval_s. The constructor determines what is emitted per object type rather than enforcing a numeric bound.
associative_links: Yes — typed graph edges across three hierarchical subgraphs (episodic, semantic entity, community). Breadth-first search traverses them at retrieval to bounded hop radius, and the paper distinguishes the three search modes by what similarity they capture (lexical / semantic / contextual-via-proximity). Communities are built by label propagation rather than Leiden, dynamically extended with periodic full refresh.
provenance: Partial and structured: the constructor returns, for each semantic edge, the fact plus its t_valid/t_invalid fields, and for each entity node the name and summary. Retrieved facts therefore carry validity dates into the prompt (the prompt template shown formats them as 'FACT (Date range: from - to)'). That is temporal provenance surfaced to the model; a pointer back to the source episode is stored in the episodic subgraph but the paper does not state that it is injected.
procedural_memory: Not specified. No procedural/skill store; memory is facts, entities and communities.
latency_cost: Author-run. Claimed accuracy improvement up to 18.5% with ~90% latency reduction vs baseline. Table 2 (their runs): Zep gpt-4o-mini 63.8% at 3.20s vs full-context 55.4% at 31.3s; Zep gpt-4o 71.2% at 2.58s vs 60.2% at 28.9s; 1.6k vs 115k avg context tokens. Important caveat the paper itself states: testing ran from a consumer laptop in Boston against AWS us-west-2, adding network latency to Zep but not to the baselines.
